findings.evidence: Lines 53–59 identify the radial curve globally with `maximalGeodesic` and invoke `pathELength_maximalGeodesic`; `Exponential.lean:127–128` characterizes exactly the needed endpoint membership, while the normal-domain data are used only at lines 57–58 to establish those endpoints.
findings.fix: First prove `pathELength ... s t = ‖v‖ₑ * ENNReal.ofReal (t-s)` assuming `s,t ∈ geodesicInterval I M p v`, then derive the normal-domain `[0,1]` and arbitrary `[s,t] ⊆ [0,1]` corollaries.
findings.issue: `pathELength_riemannianExp_smul_zero_one` only treats `[0,1]` under `IsNormalDomain`, although the same proof gives any `s,t` where the radial geodesic exists; this omits the advertised subinterval formula and makes the primary API stronger than necessary.

summary: The radial-length API is restricted to the full interval and an unnecessarily strong normal-domain hypothesis instead of exposing the natural endpoint-general result.
